It does not remove the need to know which consumers exist; background jobs and support tools are part of the compatibility graph.

topics.title: 15.2.2 Contracting Only After the Old Dependency Is Gone
topics.summary: The contraction removes old fields, compatibility paths, or storage. It should occur only after the deployment and retention window no longer requires them. A recently upgraded server can still hold old pending messages, old snapshots, or clients that reconnect infrequently.

topics.title: 15.3.1 Owning the Migration and Its Transaction Boundary
topics.summary: Choose who runs the migration. If every replica automatically attempts schema changes on startup, simultaneous deployment can create contention and confusing failures. A dedicated migration step or an explicitly serialized startup protocol can make ownership clearer.

reading.title: 15.3.1 Owning the Migration and Its Transaction Boundary
paragraphs: Choose who runs the migration. If every replica automatically attempts schema changes on startup, simultaneous deployment can create contention and confusing failures. A dedicated migration step or an explicitly serialized startup protocol can make ownership clearer.

Some database changes can be transactional under the selected engine and version; others require different operational handling. Consult the actual database documentation rather than assuming that every ALTER operation has identical locking, rewrite, or rollback behavior across products. PostgreSQL’s transaction isolation documentation illustrates why concurrent transaction behavior must be understood at the chosen engine’s level. (R23)

The chapter’s SQLite example performs a small additive migration in a controlled, in-memory database. It is not a performance claim about altering a large production table. Real migrations need a preflight that checks free storage, backup validity, expected lock duration, client compatibility, and abort conditions.

A migration identifier should be immutable once applied. Editing the text of an already recorded migration makes different environments claim the same version while holding different schemas. Add a new migration and preserve the history, including its source revision or checksum.

reading.title: Engineering case — Roll out an operation-version field without changing old jobs
paragraphs: Version 1 computes the square of an input. A proposed version 2 introduces a different calculation. Reusing the same input field and changing the worker implementation would make old pending jobs execute under new semantics. It would also make a retry conflict with a result produced before deployment.

Expand the stored and wire representation with an explicit operation version. Existing rows receive the documented version 1 interpretation. New readers understand both versions before new writers are allowed to emit version 2. The worker’s duplicate comparison includes the operation version as part of canonical meaning.

A compatibility matrix now has useful entries. An old worker can process version 1 and must reject version 2. A new worker can process both. A new gateway must not route version 2 to an old worker without capability selection. An old gateway must continue interpreting version 1 results correctly during the mixed interval.

Backfilling the version field should be repeatable and should not recalculate existing results under the new formula. The migration assigns meaning to historical rows; it does not reinterpret them. A test fixture containing a completed version 1 receipt is therefore essential.

Only after old producers, readers, retained messages, and recovery tools no longer require the old representation can contraction be considered. Even then, retaining the ability to interpret historical receipts may remain necessary for audit and replay. “No current client sends version 1” is not the same as “no persisted version 1 data exists.”

Rollback must also preserve this graph. If version 2 jobs have been accepted, restoring an old worker that rejects them can leave durable obligations pending. That may be an acceptable temporary degraded mode under a plan, but it is not a transparent rollback. A forward-compatible repair may be safer than attempting to erase the new jobs.

The shipped capstone intentionally supports only its original operation. This case is a design exercise for extending that contract. It demonstrates why semantic versioning of work matters more than merely incrementing a package version or adding a release label to logs.
